notes: Added: · Sidebar group titles ("Setup", "Design", "Ship", "Defaults", "Queue", "Beat", …) are now clickable: one click expands or collapses every panel in that group — if anything in the group is open it all collapses, otherwise it all expands — with a small chevron on the title showing the group's state (still under "reduce motion"). Alt+click (or middle-click) on a title solos that group: every other group collapses while the clicked one stays exactly as it is. · Changed: · The home screen's Recent cards now share the big page tiles' recipe: a solid translucent panel with a real border and rounded corners instead of a bare flat row, brightening with the accent colour on hover. · Fixed: · Dialogs now render reliably on Windows: their entrance no longer depends on the compositor delivering a final animation frame, and dimmed backdrops no longer use a blur filter — WebView2 could drop that frame for content inside a blurred layer, leaving the dialog invisible behind a backdrop that looked like a frozen app (the profile-delete freeze). Notification pills got the same treatment, so a toast can never render as an empty capsule. · Confirmation dialogs (deleting a profile, refusing unsaved work) now always appear centred in the window; previously they could render off-screen behind a frozen-looking backdrop whenever the window's page area didn't match the viewport. · Any dialog that can be dismissed by its buttons can now also be dismissed with Escape or by clicking the dimmed area around it — a stuck dialog can no longer trap the app. · Renaming a profile no longer pushes its Save/Cancel buttons past the panel edge on narrow sidebars — the editing row now shrinks with the panel like the display row already did. · Tooltips now appear reliably: they no longer vanish when the cursor re-enters a control within a fraction of a second, they follow faster when you move between nearby controls, disabled buttons show theirs again (hover events never reached those controls — an invisible wrapper now carries the tooltip while a button is disabled), and a tooltip no longer outlives the window losing focus or a tap on a touch screen. · Pressing a checkbox no longer flashes it empty mid-press: a checked box now darkens its fill while held instead of swapping to the empty tint, and the tick springs in with a slight overshoot instead of scaling in flat (both stay still under "reduce motion").
